w1.said: three p p is a 3D graphics library for C plus plus, modelled on three J S, the most used 3D library on the web.

w2.said: It also comes as a Python package, with the same names and the same ideas.

b1.said: Every three p p program starts the same way: a canvas, which is the window, and a renderer that draws into it.

b2.said: The scene holds everything that will be drawn.

b3.said: The camera decides where we look from, and how wide the view is.

b4.said: A mesh is two things. Its geometry is the shape: points, joined into triangles.

b5.said: Its material decides how the surface looks. Without any light, it stays black.

b6.said: So add a light, and the material shades the box: bright where it faces the light.

b7.said: Last, the render loop: each frame, update the scene and draw it. That is a complete program.

p1.said: The Python version reads almost line for line the same, and draws the very same pixels.

s1.said: In C plus plus, every create returns a shared pointer. So eight cubes can share one geometry and one material.

s2.said: Change the shared material once, and all eight cubes change with it. The GPU keeps a single copy.

s3.said: Nobody calls delete: when the last reference goes, the memory is freed. Python's references work the same way.

g1.said: Objects form a tree, the scene graph. These two moons are children of the box.

g2.said: Move or turn a parent, and its children come along. Positions are relative to the parent.

m1.said: Materials decide how a surface answers light: from Basic, which ignores light, to Standard and Physical, which follow real physics.

m2.said: Lights come in several kinds too: directional like the sun, point like a bulb, spotlights, and soft sky light.

r1.said: Loaders turn files into the same kind of tree: G L T F, O B J, S T L, and robots from U R D F. This arm is 191 objects.

r2.said: Beyond three J S there are tools for robotics. The inverse kinematics solver moves the hand onto the target, frame after frame.

f1.said: With [PhysX](/fˈɪzˌɛks/) built in, add meshes to a physics world and step it. The meshes follow the simulation.

d1.said: Simulated sensors see the same scene. This depth camera returns about 17,000 points per scan, each a 3D position.

v1.said: Everything so far was drawn by the Open G L renderer, which runs almost anywhere. An optional Vulkan renderer adds ray-traced light, water and particles.

t1.said: To start in C plus plus, pull three p p into your C Make project with Fetch Content. For Python, it is pip install three p p.

t2.said: Then read the getting started guide, and run the examples. Each one is a small program to learn from.
